subsystems.name: Chassis organism
subsystems.role: the base cell whose genome is stripped down and rewired for extreme conditions.

subsystems.name: Genetic circuits
subsystems.role: sense and respond to stresses such as radiation, desiccation or temperature swings.

subsystems.name: Stress-hardening systems
subsystems.role: protect proteins and DNA from damage.

subsystems.name: Alternative biochemistry
subsystems.role: non-standard genetic polymers or amino acids that resist degradation and prevent escape.

subsystems.name: Containment
subsystems.role: keep the organism alive only under controlled conditions.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target environment
buildSteps.detail: Define the exact stress — high radiation, vacuum, extreme pH, low temperature — and identify natural extremophiles that already cope with it.

buildSteps.title: Design the genome
buildSteps.detail: Use computational models to design metabolic pathways and regulatory circuits that function under those stresses.

buildSteps.title: Synthesize DNA
buildSteps.detail: Chemically synthesize the designed genes and assemble them into large DNA constructs.

buildSteps.title: Build or edit the chassis
buildSteps.detail: Either edit a robust host with CRISPR or attempt to synthesize a minimal genome from scratch.

buildSteps.title: Iterate design–build–test
buildSteps.detail: Grow the organism in simulated extreme conditions, select the best survivors and repeat the cycle.

buildSteps.title: Add containment
buildSteps.detail: Insert kill switches and make the organism dependent on a non-natural nutrient so it cannot spread.

buildSteps.title: Scale production
buildSteps.detail: Grow the engineered organism in controlled bioreactors, optimising temperature, feed and waste removal.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Release into the target setting — bioremediation, industrial waste or space — with sensors tracking survival and genetic stability.

prerequisites.why: large designed genomes must be built from scratch or heavily edited.
precise changes to existing organisms are needed to add or remove traits.
only a few minimal bacterial genomes have been built, and none are extremophiles.
many natural stress-tolerance mechanisms are known but cannot yet be transferred reliably.
XNA can store information in test tubes but has not yet sustained a living cell.
kill switches exist but can fail through mutation, so safe release is unproven.

pathway.milestone: engineer natural extremophiles for industrial enzymes and space research
pathway.unlocks: better catalysts and organisms for harsh conditions.

pathway.milestone: synthetic minimal cells with added stress resistance
pathway.unlocks: a platform for stacking multiple extreme traits in one organism.

pathway.milestone: organisms with alternative genetic systems (XNA) for biocontainment
pathway.unlocks: safe deployment in open environments without horizontal gene transfer.

pathway.milestone: fully synthetic organisms designed for extreme environments such as Mars or high-radiation waste
pathway.unlocks: new capabilities in space settlement and bioremediation.
